ai.description: *Micryletta aishani* is a small, stout frog (22–27 mm) with a reddish-brown dorsum and dark lateral markings. It is distinguished by a rounded snout and a distinct, dark hourglass-shaped dorsal pattern.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Micryletta aishani* is best distinguished from other Indian congeners by its distinct, dark-brown, hourglass-shaped dorsal pattern that narrows significantly at the mid-body.
ai.habitat: *Micryletta aishani* inhabits the tropical evergreen and semi-evergreen forests of Northeast India, typically found in leaf litter at elevations between 200 and 1,100 meters.
ai.behavior: The *Micryletta aishani* is primarily nocturnal, emerging from leaf litter after dark to forage for small invertebrates during the rainy season.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Micryletta aishani* is an explosive breeder that lays eggs in temporary rain pools during the monsoon season (May–June), producing clutches of approximately 100–200 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Micryletta aishani* is endemic to Northeast India, specifically found in the states of Assam and Tripura across low-to-mid elevation forest habitats.
ai.callDescription: The *Micryletta aishani* produces a high-pitched, insect-like "tink-tink" call, typically emitted by males from shallow, rain-filled pools in paddy fields and forest edges.
